subject: hamerkop bird
title: This Small Brown Bird Builds a Nest Strong Enough to Hold a Man

scenes.text: A bird the size of a crow builds a nest you could stand on.
The hamerkop of Africa piles up around 8,000 sticks, glued with mud.
The dome can reach two metres across, with a tunnel entrance and a hidden chamber.
Then it builds another. Pairs in Mali made three to four nests a year.
Why so many? Barn owls, eagle-owls, geese and snakes keep moving in and taking over.
So the hamerkop keeps building the biggest houses in the woods, mostly for everyone else.

description:
The hamerkop, a crow-sized African wading bird, builds a domed nest of around 8,000 sticks that can reach 2 metres across and support a person's weight.
Pairs build several nests a year, and barn owls, Verreaux's eagle-owls, Egyptian geese, snakes and genets often take them over.
Which animal would you evict first?
first_comment: A review found 20 other bird species using hamerkop nests, barn owls most of all. Which squatter would you kick out first?
